name: Triund
summary: The classic first Himalayan trek: a short, steady climb to a grassy ridge facing the Dhauladhar wall.

risky.reason: Monsoon: the trail is slippery and the approach roads see landslides.
Snow on the upper trail and sub-zero nights. Go with a local guide.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares, campsite listings and trek operator rates

safety_notes: Start the climb before 10 am so you reach the top with daylight to spare.
Overnight camping rules on Triund ridge have changed over the years. Use a registered campsite and check with the forest office in Dharamshala.
Leave the ridge immediately if a thunderstorm builds; it is fully exposed to lightning.
permit_notes: No permit needed for Indian citizens.

plan.title: McLeodganj to Triund
plan.detail: Arrive by overnight bus. Breakfast, then trek via Galu Devi temple (9 km, about 4–5 h). Sunset over the Kangra valley and camp on the ridge.

plan.title: Sunrise and descent
plan.detail: Sunrise over the Dhauladhars, descend to McLeodganj, lunch at Bhagsu and take the evening bus home.

extras.title: Snowline Café and Laka Got
extras.detail: Day hike up to Snowline (3,100 m) for close views of the glacier, back to camp at Triund.

name: Kheerganga
summary: A forest trail along the Parvati river to a meadow with a natural hot spring at the top.

risky.reason: Monsoon landslides on the Bhuntar–Barshaini road and slippery forest trail.
Cold nights and most camps start closing for winter.

closed.reason: Snow on the trail and the camps at the top are shut.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares, campsite listings and trek operator rates

safety_notes: Take the Nakthan (left bank) trail. It is longer but safer than the Rudranag route after rain.
Camping on the meadow is regulated by court orders; stay only in registered camps or dhabas.
Carry your plastic back down. The meadow has no waste collection.
permit_notes: No permit needed for Indian citizens.

plan.title: Barshaini to Kheerganga
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Bhuntar, local bus to Barshaini. Trek via Nakthan village (12 km, 5–6 h). Evening dip in the hot spring.

plan.title: Descent and home
plan.detail: Sunrise over the Parvati valley, descend to Barshaini, cafés at Kasol, evening bus from Bhuntar.

extras.title: Slow day at Kheerganga
extras.detail: Stay a second night. Short walk above the meadow and a quiet evening by the spring.

name: Hampta Pass
summary: A crossover trek from green Kullu meadows to the stark, desert landscape of Lahaul.

risky.reason: Early snowfall can bury the pass, and nights drop well below freezing.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and trek operator package rates

safety_notes: Go with a registered operator or a guide. Weather on the pass changes within an hour.
River crossings near Balu ka Ghera are safest before noon, when snowmelt is lowest.
Headache with nausea at Balu ka Ghera is early altitude sickness. Do not go higher until it clears.
permit_notes: A forest department trekking permit is usually arranged by your operator.

plan.title: Manali to Chika
plan.detail: Drive to Jobra, then an easy trek through pine and maple forest to the Chika campsite.

plan.title: Chika to Balu ka Ghera
plan.detail: Follow the Hampta river through meadows, with a couple of stream crossings.

plan.title: Over Hampta Pass to Shea Goru
plan.detail: Start at dawn, cross the pass at 4,270 m and descend steeply into Lahaul.

plan.title: Shea Goru to Chatru, drive to Manali
plan.detail: Descend to Chatru on the Chandra river, then drive back to Manali through the Atal Tunnel. Night bus home.

extras.title: Acclimatisation day at Balu ka Ghera
extras.detail: Short hike towards the pass and back. This makes pass day much easier.

name: Bir Billing
summary: India's paragliding capital: a Tibetan colony with monasteries, cafés and tandem flights from Billing.

risky.reason: Hot, strong midday thermals. Fly only in morning slots with a certified pilot.
Paragliding is usually suspended from mid-July to mid-September.
Cold, with short flying windows that depend on the weather.

cost.source: Team estimate from bus fares, homestay listings and tandem flight operator rates

safety_notes: Fly only with pilots registered with the HP tourism department, and ask to see their licence.
Check that the operator gives you a helmet and a harness with a reserve parachute.
The Billing road is narrow and steep. Use operator transport rather than driving yourself.
permit_notes: No permit needed. Your flight operator handles flying permissions.

plan.title: Arrive in Bir
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Bir. Walk through the Tibetan colony and Chokling monastery, with sunset at the landing site.

plan.title: Tandem flight from Billing
plan.detail: Morning drive to the Billing take-off at 2,400 m for a 15–25 minute tandem flight. Cafés, then the evening bus home.

extras.title: Billing and Rajgundha meadows
extras.detail: Drive up to Billing and hike towards Rajgundha's meadows, then come back to Bir for the night.

name: Kasol & Manikaran
summary: Riverside cafés in the Parvati valley, with the Manikaran gurudwara and its hot springs next door.

risky.reason: Landslides and flash floods on the Bhuntar–Kasol road during monsoon.
Cold, and many cafés and guesthouses close for winter.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and guesthouse listings

safety_notes: Don't sit on the riverbank rocks; the Parvati rises fast without warning.
Solo travellers: stick to well-reviewed guesthouses and share your stay details with someone at home.
Narcotics possession is a serious offence under the NDPS Act, and police checks are frequent.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Kasol and Chalal
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Bhuntar, local bus to Kasol. Riverside walk to Chalal village and evening cafés.

plan.title: Manikaran Sahib
plan.detail: Visit the gurudwara, community langar and hot springs at Manikaran, then the evening bus from Bhuntar.

extras.title: Rasol village hike
extras.detail: Stiff climb from Chalal to Rasol (2,150 m) through forest, then back down to Kasol.

name: Spiti Valley (Kinnaur route)
summary: A high-altitude cold desert of monasteries, fossil villages and the world's highest post office.

risky.reason: Frequent landslides on NH-5 in Kinnaur during monsoon. Spiti itself stays dry.
Nights below 0 °C, and Kunzum may be shut, so travel via Kinnaur both ways.
Winter Spiti: −15 to −25 °C, frozen pipes and road blocks. Go only with an experienced driver and full winter gear.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares, shared taxi rates and homestay listings

safety_notes: Ascend slowly through Kinnaur. Going straight from Shimla to Kaza in one go is the commonest cause of altitude sickness here.
ATMs and mobile networks are sparse beyond Reckong Peo, so carry cash. BSNL and Jio work in Kaza town.
Fuel up at Reckong Peo and Kaza; there are no pumps in between.
permit_notes: No permit needed for Indian citizens. Foreign nationals need an Inner Line Permit for parts of the Kinnaur route.

plan.title: Shimla to Kalpa
plan.detail: Arrive in Shimla early and drive along the Sutlej through Narkanda and Rampur to Kalpa, facing Kinner Kailash.

plan.title: Kalpa to Tabo via Nako
plan.detail: Into the cold desert: Nako lake and village, then Tabo's thousand-year-old monastery.

plan.title: Tabo to Pin Valley
plan.detail: Dhankar monastery on its cliff, then into Pin Valley National Park to Mud village.

plan.title: Pin Valley to Kaza
plan.detail: Drive to Kaza, then Key monastery and Kibber village in the evening.

plan.title: Langza, Hikkim and Komic
plan.detail: Fossil village of Langza, the world's highest post office at Hikkim, and Komic at 4,587 m. Back to Kaza.

plan.title: Kaza to Kalpa
plan.detail: Long drive back down through Kinnaur.

plan.title: Kalpa to Shimla
plan.detail: Drive to Shimla and take the night bus home.

extras.title: Rest day in Kaza
extras.detail: Slow day in Kaza's market and cafés to let your body adjust to 3,800 m.

extras.title: Dhankar Lake hike
extras.detail: A steep hike from Dhankar village to a high lake, then back to Kaza.

name: Chandratal Lake
summary: A crescent-shaped high-altitude lake whose colour shifts from turquoise to deep blue through the day.

risky.reason: Camps start closing in early October and nights drop to −5 °C.

closed.reason: Snowbound and the camps are closed.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares, shared taxi rates and camp listings

safety_notes: Manali to Chandratal is a jump of more than 2,000 m in one day. Watch for headache, nausea or breathlessness at night.
The Batal–Chandratal stretch has stream crossings that swell in the afternoon. Cross early.
Camping is not allowed at the lakeshore itself. Camps are about 2 km away.
permit_notes: No permit needed when travelling via the Atal Tunnel.

plan.title: Manali to Chandratal
plan.detail: Early start through the Atal Tunnel, Gramphu and Batal on a rough road to the camps near the lake.

plan.title: Lake walk and back to Manali
plan.detail: Walk the lake circuit at sunrise, then drive back to Manali for the night bus.

extras.title: Second night at Chandratal
extras.detail: Spend another day at the lake for sunrise light and a night of stargazing.

name: Prashar Lake
summary: A sacred lake with a floating island and a pagoda temple, set on a ridge with 360° Himalayan views.

risky.reason: Slippery trail and landslides on the Mandi–Baggi road.
Snow can block the road, and nights are well below freezing.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and rest-house/camp listings

safety_notes: The temple area is sacred. No alcohol, and don't enter the lake.
The ridge is exposed. Head down if dark clouds build in the afternoon.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Mandi to Prashar
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Mandi, local bus to Baggi, then trek up through forest to the lake (7 km). Sunset from the ridge.

plan.title: Sunrise and descent
plan.detail: Sunrise over the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges, visit the temple, descend to Baggi and take the bus home from Mandi.

extras.title: Ridge walk
extras.detail: Walk the ridge north of the lake for views of the Kullu valley, then spend a second night at the lake.

name: Jibhi & Serolsar Lake
summary: Wooden village homestays in the Tirthan side valley, plus a forest walk from Jalori Pass to Serolsar Lake.

risky.reason: Monsoon: landslides on the Aut–Banjar road.
Jalori Pass road is often shut by snow, so Serolsar may be unreachable.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and homestay listings

safety_notes: The Jalori road has hairpin bends at a steep gradient. Take a local taxi rather than driving yourself.
Black bears live in the forest near Serolsar. Walk in groups and make noise on the trail.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Arrive in Jibhi
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Aut, taxi to Jibhi. Walk to Jibhi waterfall and settle into a wooden homestay.

plan.title: Jalori Pass to Serolsar
plan.detail: Drive to Jalori Pass (3,120 m), walk 5 km through oak forest to Serolsar Lake and back. Evening bus home from Aut.

extras.title: Chehni Kothi
extras.detail: Hike to the 1,500-year-old Chehni Kothi tower above Shrikot village.

extras.title: Shoja and Raghupur Fort
extras.detail: Ridge walk from Jalori to the ruins of Raghupur Fort, with meadow views of the Greater Himalaya.

name: Bhrigu Lake
summary: A short, steep trek to an alpine lake above Manali that stays frozen into June.

risky.reason: Monsoon brings fog, rain and slippery meadow slopes.

closed.reason: Deep snow; the trail is not safely marked.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and trek operator package rates

safety_notes: The gain from Gulaba to Rola Kholi is steep. Go slowly and drink 3–4 litres of water a day.
Turn back from the lake by 1 pm; afternoon fog makes the meadow route hard to follow.
permit_notes: A forest department trekking permit is usually arranged by your operator.

plan.title: Manali to Rola Kholi
plan.detail: Drive to Gulaba, then a steep climb through meadows to the Rola Kholi camp.

plan.title: Bhrigu Lake summit day
plan.detail: Climb to the lake at 4,235 m with views of the Pir Panjal range, then return to camp.

plan.title: Descend to Manali
plan.detail: Back to Gulaba and Manali. Evening night bus home.

extras.title: Acclimatisation day at Rola Kholi
extras.detail: Short walk above camp and back, so summit day is easier.

name: Kareri Lake
summary: A quiet riverside trek through Gaddi shepherd country to a shallow glacial lake.

risky.reason: The Nyund stream crossings become dangerous in monsoon.

closed.reason: The lake freezes and the upper trail is under snow.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and local guide rates

safety_notes: Hire a guide from Kareri village. The trail splits several times along the river.
Shepherd dogs guard the flocks. Give them space and don't run.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Dharamshala to Rioti
plan.detail: Taxi to Ghera, then follow the Nyund stream up through Kareri village to the Rioti meadow.

plan.title: Rioti to Kareri Lake
plan.detail: Short climb to the lake and the small Shiva temple, then explore the shoreline.

plan.title: Back to Dharamshala
plan.detail: Long descent to Ghera, taxi to Dharamshala and the night bus home.

extras.title: Towards Minkiani Pass
extras.detail: Day hike up the ridge towards Minkiani Pass for Dhauladhar views, then back to the lake.

name: Beas Kund
summary: The glacial source of the Beas river, in an amphitheatre under Hanuman Tibba and Friendship Peak.

risky.reason: Monsoon: rockfall on the moraine and swollen streams.

closed.reason: Under snow, with avalanche risk on the moraine.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and trek operator package rates

safety_notes: Walk on the moraine in single file and don't stop under loose boulder slopes.
Solang is crowded with adventure sports. Book only with operators registered with HP tourism.
permit_notes: A forest department trekking permit is usually arranged by your operator.

plan.title: Manali to Bakarthach
plan.detail: Drive to Solang and Dhundi, then trek along the Beas to the Bakarthach meadow.

plan.title: Beas Kund and back
plan.detail: Cross the moraine to the glacial lake at 3,700 m and return to camp.

plan.title: Descend to Manali
plan.detail: Walk out to Solang, drive to Manali and take the night bus.

extras.title: Night at Beas Kund
extras.detail: Camp at the lake for sunrise on Hanuman Tibba.

name: Tosh
summary: A terraced village at the end of the Parvati road, facing snow peaks and the Tosh glacier.

risky.reason: Landslides on the Barshaini road during monsoon.
Snowfall, very cold nights and few guesthouses open.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and guesthouse listings

safety_notes: Respect village customs: ask before photographing people or entering temples.
Narcotics possession is a serious offence under the NDPS Act, and police checks are frequent in this valley.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Barshaini to Tosh
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Bhuntar, local bus to Barshaini and a short climb to Tosh. Sunset over the glacier.

plan.title: Tosh valley walk and home
plan.detail: Morning walk up the Tosh valley towards Kutla, then back down and the evening bus home.

extras.title: Pulga and the Fairy Forest
extras.detail: Cross to Pulga and wander through its old deodar forest, then come back to Tosh.

name: Tirthan Valley & GHNP
summary: A trout river valley that serves as the gateway to the Great Himalayan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

risky.reason: Monsoon: GHNP trails are often closed and the river rises fast.
Cold, and the upper park trails are under snow.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares, homestay listings and GHNP fee notices

safety_notes: Enter GHNP only with a park entry permit and, for overnight routes, a registered local guide.
Trout fishing needs a licence from the fisheries department, and catch-and-release is encouraged.
permit_notes: Great Himalayan National Park entry permit (about ₹50–₹100 for Indians, estimate); fishing licence extra.

plan.title: Arrive in Gushaini
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Aut, taxi to Gushaini. Riverside walk and trout for dinner.

plan.title: GHNP day hike to Rolla
plan.detail: Pick up your park permit, then hike through the park buffer zone to Rolla and back.

plan.title: Bathad and home
plan.detail: Slow morning in Bathad village, then the evening bus from Aut.

extras.title: Slow day in Gushaini
extras.detail: Village walk, local food and a rest day by the river.

extras.title: Serolsar from Jalori
extras.detail: Day trip to Jalori Pass and the forest walk to Serolsar Lake.

name: Narkanda & Hatu Peak
summary: Apple orchards and a forest walk up to the Hatu temple, with a skiing slope in winter.

risky.reason: Monsoon landslides on NH-5.
Snow and black ice on the Shimla–Narkanda road. Great for snow lovers, but drive with locals.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and hotel listings

safety_notes: In winter, carry snow chains or use a local taxi; black ice on the road is the main risk.
Hatu Peak is exposed. Don't stay on top during a thunderstorm.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Shimla to Narkanda
plan.detail: Arrive in Shimla early and take a bus to Narkanda through cedar forest. Evening walk through the orchards.

plan.title: Hatu Peak and home
plan.detail: Walk through the forest to the Hatu Mata temple at 3,400 m, back to Narkanda and the bus home via Shimla.

extras.title: Tannu Jubbar Lake
extras.detail: Short trip to Tannu Jubbar Lake and the orchard villages, for apples in autumn or the ski slopes in winter.

name: Chitkul & Sangla
summary: The last inhabited village before the Tibet border, on the Baspa river with wooden Kinnauri houses.

risky.reason: Frequent landslides on NH-5 in Kinnaur during monsoon.
Cold, early or late snow, and fewer guesthouses open.

closed.reason: Heavy snow often blocks the Sangla–Chitkul road and most guesthouses shut.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares, shared taxi rates and homestay listings

safety_notes: Karcham to Sangla is one of the most landslide-prone roads in the state. Travel in daylight only.
Chitkul has very limited mobile signal; tell someone your plan before leaving Sangla.
permit_notes: No permit needed for Indian citizens. Foreign nationals should check current Inner Line Permit rules for Kinnaur.

plan.title: Shimla to Sangla
plan.detail: Arrive in Shimla early and drive along the Sutlej, then up the Baspa valley to Sangla.

plan.title: Sangla to Chitkul
plan.detail: Short drive to Chitkul. Walk along the Baspa river and visit the Mathi temple.

plan.title: Chitkul to Kalpa
plan.detail: Drive to Kalpa for sunset on Kinner Kailash, and walk to Roghi village.

plan.title: Kalpa to Shimla
plan.detail: Long drive back to Shimla and the night bus home.

extras.title: Nagasti and the Baspa meadows
extras.detail: Walk up the valley towards the Nagasti ITBP post and the riverside meadows.

extras.title: Slow morning in Kalpa
extras.detail: Rest day with Kinner Kailash views and apple orchards.

name: Dalhousie & Khajjiar
summary: A colonial hill station and the forest-ringed Khajjiar meadow, with an easy wildlife walk in Kalatop.

risky.reason: Heavy monsoon rain and landslides on the Pathankot road.
Snow can block the Khajjiar road.

cost.source: Team estimate from train/bus fares and hotel listings

safety_notes: Kalatop is a wildlife sanctuary; stay on the marked forest road and walk only in daylight.
Horse rides at Khajjiar are unregulated. Agree on the price before you get on.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Arrive in Dalhousie
plan.detail: Overnight train or bus to Pathankot, then a bus to Dalhousie. Walk to the old churches and along Mall Road.

plan.title: Kalatop and Khajjiar
plan.detail: Forest walk through Kalatop sanctuary, then the Khajjiar meadow and lake. Evening bus to Pathankot.

extras.title: Dainkund Peak
extras.detail: Hike to Pohlani Mata temple on Dainkund peak (2,755 m), the highest point near Dalhousie.

name: Barot Valley
summary: An offbeat river valley with trout farms, a 1920s haulage trolley line and the Nargu wildlife sanctuary.

risky.reason: Monsoon landslides on the Ghatasani–Barot road.
Snowfall can block the road from Ghatasani.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and homestay listings

safety_notes: Water is released from the Barot reservoir without warning. Stay off riverbed rocks.
Nargu sanctuary has black bears; walk in groups and avoid dusk.
permit_notes: No permit needed. Fishing needs a licence from the fisheries department.

plan.title: Mandi to Barot
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Mandi, then a bus via Ghatasani to Barot. Riverside walk and the trout farm.

plan.title: Lohardi and home
plan.detail: Walk along the Uhl river to Lohardi village and back, then the evening bus via Mandi.

extras.title: Polling village and the trolley line
extras.detail: Hike up to Polling village along the old haulage trolley line.

name: Churdhar Peak
summary: The highest peak in the outer Himalaya, with a Shiva temple on top and views stretching to the Gangetic plains.

risky.reason: Monsoon fog, leeches and lightning on the summit ridge.

closed.reason: Snow on the trail; the temple and sarai close for winter.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and temple sarai donations

safety_notes: Summit day is long. Start before 6 am and carry a headlamp.
The summit is a lightning hotspot, so descend at the first sign of a storm.
Churdhar is a wildlife sanctuary; follow the temple trail and carry back all waste.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Nohradhar to Churdhar sarai
plan.detail: Overnight bus via Solan to Nohradhar, then a long forest trek to the temple sarai below the summit.

plan.title: Summit sunrise and descent
plan.detail: Sunrise from the summit at 3,647 m, then descend to Nohradhar for the bus home.

extras.title: Second night near the summit
extras.detail: Rest at the sarai and catch both sunset and sunrise from the top.

name: Indrahar Pass
summary: A steep, rocky pass across the Dhauladhar ridge, with views down into Chamba and across to the Pir Panjal.

risky.reason: Monsoon whiteouts, slippery rock and lightning on the ridge.
Early snow can make the final boulder section technical.

closed.reason: The pass is under snow and needs mountaineering gear.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and trek operator package rates

safety_notes: The final 300 m is boulder scrambling. Don't attempt it without a guide who knows the route.
Water is scarce above Lahesh Caves, so carry 3 litres per person on summit day.
permit_notes: A forest department trekking permit is usually arranged by your operator.

plan.title: McLeodganj to Laka Got
plan.detail: Trek past Triund and Snowline to the Laka Got campsite below the glacier.

plan.title: Laka Got to Lahesh Caves
plan.detail: Short, steep climb to the rock shelters at Lahesh.

plan.title: Indrahar Pass and back
plan.detail: Pre-dawn start, boulder scramble to the pass at 4,342 m, then return to Lahesh.

plan.title: Descend to McLeodganj
plan.detail: Long descent via Triund. Evening bus home.

extras.title: Acclimatisation at Lahesh Caves
extras.detail: Rest and a short hike above the caves before the pass push.

name: Pin Parvati Pass
summary: A serious high-altitude expedition from the green Parvati valley over a glaciated 5,319 m pass into Spiti.

risky.reason: Heavy snow cover on the pass hides crevasses, and storms come early or late in the season.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC fares and expedition operator package rates

safety_notes: Do not attempt this without a registered expedition outfit, a rope team and glacier gear.
You need prior experience of at least one 4,500 m+ trek.
There is no network for 7 days. Carry a satellite messenger or an OFFGRID beacon.
permit_notes: Forest and wildlife permits for the Great Himalayan National Park buffer and Pin Valley National Park; your outfit arranges them.

plan.title: Barshaini to Kheerganga
plan.detail: Start the expedition on the Kheerganga trail.

plan.title: Kheerganga to Tunda Bhuj
plan.detail: Into the upper Parvati valley.

plan.title: Tunda Bhuj to Thakur Kuan
plan.detail: Meadows and boulder fields along the river.

plan.title: Thakur Kuan to Odi Thach
plan.detail: Cross the natural rock bridge at Pandu Pul.

plan.title: Odi Thach to Mantalai
plan.detail: Reach the sacred Mantalai lake, the source of the Parvati.

plan.title: Mantalai to Base Camp
plan.detail: Steep climb onto moraine to the pass base camp.

plan.title: Over Pin Parvati Pass
plan.detail: Rope up across the glacier to the 5,319 m pass, then descend to the Pin side.

plan.title: Pin side to Mud village
plan.detail: Long walk down the Pin valley to Mud.

plan.title: Mud to Manali via Kunzum
plan.detail: Drive via Kaza and Kunzum Pass to Manali, then the night bus home.

extras.title: Acclimatise at Mantalai
extras.detail: Rest day and a short hike above the lake before the big climb.

extras.title: Weather buffer day
extras.detail: Pass crossings often slip a day because of weather, so keep this in reserve.

name: Chandrakhani Pass
summary: Meadows and deodar forest above Naggar, rising to a pass with views of the Pir Panjal and Parvati ranges.

risky.reason: Monsoon: slippery meadow slopes and leeches lower down.
Lingering or early snow near the pass and freezing nights.

cost.source: Team estimate from HRTC/Volvo fares and trek operator package rates

safety_notes: The trail forks towards Malana. Malana has strict local customs about touching people and property, so don't descend that way without a guide.
Meadows above Rumsu are exposed. Plan to be off the pass by early afternoon.
permit_notes: No permit needed.

plan.title: Naggar to Rumsu meadows
plan.detail: Overnight bus to Kullu, taxi to Naggar and Rumsu village, then climb through deodar forest to a meadow camp.

plan.title: Chandrakhani Pass and back
plan.detail: Climb to the pass at 3,660 m for views of Deo Tibba, and return to camp.

plan.title: Descend to Naggar
plan.detail: Walk down to Rumsu and Naggar, visit Naggar Castle, then the night bus from Kullu.

extras.title: Slow day in the meadows
extras.detail: Extra night in the meadows. Explore the ridge and watch the shepherds bring their flocks in.
